A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AccelAes and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the added sections, renumbered tables, and relocated references.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality and runtime measurements on three DiT backbones, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and anchor-coverage analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds human preference judgments, prompt and scene robustness experiments, distilled-model evaluation, and mask-refresh and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The core algorithm and Equations (1)-(13) remain unchanged. However, v1 Appendix E.3 specifies uniform-token fallback below anchor similarity 0.60, while v2 Appendix F.3 explicitly retains top-r selection without that fallback, resolving a conflict with the existing main-text description. v2 also introduces delayed-mask and entropy-based corrective variants for failures, although their precise rules remain underspecified.

E1.justification: v2 adds controlled descriptor-free versus descriptor-added prompts and targeted difficult-scene and non-centric scenarios, including crowds, clutter, and abstract art (Tables 14-15 and 18). These extend tested input conditions within the retained text-to-image task; the original Pick-a-Pic evaluation remains.

E2.justification: The original per-backbone comparator sets are retained. New comparisons include dense generation, FORA, and a variant without Spatial CFG in the human study, plus dense generation and TaylorSeer in the FLUX.1-schnell test. These are limited comparison extensions without a new external acceleration method.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a randomized blind study with 15 annotators, 60 pairs, four questions, and tie-excluding win rates; a 200-base-prompt wording experiment; static, five-step, and per-step mask-refresh controls; and a four-step FLUX.1-schnell evaluation. These substantially expand evaluation design. The original 10,000-prompt protocol and 30/28-step backbone settings remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component, token-weighting, sparsity, and mask-timing ablations, v2 adds descriptor and complex-scene robustness, a human comparison without Spatial CFG, static-versus-dynamic masks, explicit masking/guidance overhead diagnostics, and mined failure cases with mitigation experiments (Section 4.3 and Appendix E). These investigate several previously untested vulnerabilities.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports binomial tests of non-tie human votes against a 50% null, stating p < 0.001 for the main comparisons except alignment against dense generation. It also specifies two seeds for the new hard-scene tests. The retained main experiments still use three fixed seeds, with no added confidence intervals for their scores.

E6.justification: v2 adds human overall win rates of 67% against dense generation, 89% against FORA, and 66% against the no-Spatial-CFG variant, alongside new robustness, distilled-model, and mask-refresh results. Existing values also change: Lumina Aesthetic score becomes 6.0414 rather than 6.1414 in Table 1, and spatial-only latency becomes 8.65 rather than 8.72 seconds in the runtime decomposition. The headline 2.11× speedup and 0.8410 ImageReward remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical method definitions and Equations (1)-(13) are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. The added p = 100q relationship explains equivalent percentile and implementation notation.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain the same claims about training-free aesthetic-aware acceleration and improved speed-quality trade-offs across three backbones, including 2.11× speedup and +11.9% ImageReward on Lumina. The revised conclusion incorporates new supporting evidence without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new evidence as showing human-perceived benefits, robustness without aesthetic adjectives, and applicability beyond centered subjects. It adds region jitter as an explanation for dynamic-mask degradation and frozen unmasked details as a failure mechanism. Appendix F also reinterprets anchor-hit statistics as vocabulary coverage rather than inference activation. These substantially expand applicability and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies the skip-ratio/percentile mapping and explicitly describes SD3's AesMask-guided spatial path with uniform CFG. The FLUX.1-dev reference gains a checkpoint URL. Hardware, precision, core cache schedules, and the project URL remain unchanged, while the statement that competing baselines use official/default cache intervals is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mao et al.'s Ctrl-Z Sampling and expands Section 2.1 to mention trajectory changes through controlled exploration. The other cited works are retained; the expanded FLUX reference identifies the same existing backbone.

P1.justification: v2 adds a human/robustness subsection and appendix, revises the conclusion and anchor-coverage explanation, fixes cross-references, and moves references before the appendices. Keywords and a corresponding-author marker are added. Most existing narrative and method prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial table suite for human judgments, robustness, overhead, distilled-model compatibility, and mask refresh (Table 3 and Tables 13-18); Table 13 repeats the main human-study results. Retained tables gain colored highlighting and some revised labels. All twelve figures are retained, with Figures 4 and 5 brought onto the same page.

improvement.justification: v1's perceptual-quality claims relied on automatic proxies and qualitative examples. v2 substantially strengthens their support through direct human judgments and targeted tests of descriptor dependence, difficult scenes, mask stability, and overhead. It also resolves the Table 1/Table 2 aesthetic-score inconsistency and conflicting anchor-selection documentation. These address important validation and clarity gaps, although some new experimental protocols and failure-mitigation parameters remain underspecified.
